references.text: Earlier verses in the same chapter describing the Midianite invasion and destruction of Israel's crops
Describes the Midianites and Amalekites lying in the valley, numerous as locusts, and their camels without number like the sand on the seashore
Mentions the size of the enemy army, emphasizing the enormous number of foes Israel faced
The plague of locusts in Egypt is used as a comparison - they covered the whole land and destroyed everything that grew
The locusts in Egypt came in such numbers that they covered the surface of the earth and ate up everything
Jeremiah compares enemies to locusts that are without number
Joel's description of the locust invasion that destroys the land resembles the ravages of the Midianites
The prophecy about a numerous people coming and destroying, compared to locusts
Reference to gathering plunder as locusts gather together
